description:
## Goal

Keep reusable-cons physical work and runtime demand consistent when a caller
ignores a list-rebuilding function's semantic return.

## Live defect at origin/main a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83

The ignored test

`compiler2::drive_test::compiler2_jit_and_backend_interp_agree_on_reusable_cons_exit_counters`

contains the minimal deterministic repro:

    fn ping(x), do: x

    fn rebuild(xs) do
      [h | t] = xs
      [h | t]
    end

    fn rebuild_after_publish(xs) do
      [h | t] = xs
      ping(xs)
      {xs, [h | t]}
    end

    fn main() do
      rebuild([1, 2])
      rebuild_after_publish([3, 4])
      0
    end

Current production-path results:

- `fz2 interp`: exit 1:
  `backend executable 2 function 32 entry 0 step evaluation failed:
  backend value 0 is unbound`
- `fz2 run`: exit 101 at `jobs/native.rs`:
  `native lowering invariant failed: backend value ValueId(0) ... must be
  bound before runtime use`
- `fz2 build`: exit 101 with the same native invariant

The backend dump makes the inconsistency explicit. `rebuild/1` has no runtime
parameter representation, runtime demand marks input 0 `ignore`, and `v0` is
not bound, but its body still retains:

    split_list v0 -> head=v1 tail=v2
    reusable_cons head=v1 source=v0

`rebuild_after_publish/1` has the corresponding absent input and retained
`SplitList` across its delivered continuation.

This is not an Enum HOF, closure-brand, or activation-specialization repro.
The original distinct-closure Enum repro is green on interp, JIT, and AOT.

## Strategy

Make the physical reusable-cons requirement participate in the same
demand/materialization decision as the retained backend operations. Every
retained `SplitList` or reusable-cons source must have a runtime binding on
both interpreter and native paths.

Do not add a native-only placeholder or weaken the bound-before-use invariant.
The backend artifact, interpreter, and native lowering must agree about whether
the physical source exists.

The existing detector defines the runtime contract for this case: both rebuilds
execute, producing two reuse attempts; the unique first source is reused and
the published/aliased second source falls back, producing one reuse.

Inspect together:

- `src/compiler2/jobs/runtime_demand.rs`
- backend layout/materialization in `src/compiler2/jobs/backend.rs`
- `BackendStep::SplitList` and reusable-cons capture lowering in
  `src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs`
- the corresponding interpreter paths in `src/ir_interp/backend.rs`

## Remove stale scope

`enum_tier0` is not a detector for this defect. With its independently failing
Map `Enum.reduce/2` line skipped, all three lanes currently complete and print
all expected values. Remove the stale `fz-k22`/unbound-value second-blocker
claim from `fixtures2/behavior/enum_tier0.fz`; leave its independent first
blocker accurately documented.

Update the ignored test's stale `fz-k22`/generic-Enum annotation to this ticket.

## Checks

- Remove `#[ignore]` from
  `compiler2_jit_and_backend_interp_agree_on_reusable_cons_exit_counters`.
- The test passes on JIT and backend interpreter with:
  - halt value `0`
  - `reusable_cons_attempts == 2`
  - `reusable_cons_reused == 1`
- The exact source above succeeds through `fz2 interp`, `fz2 run`, and
  `fz2 build` plus execution.
- These existing focused tests remain green:
  - `compiler2_reusable_cons_runtime_telemetry_reports_in_place_reuse`
  - `compiler2_reusable_cons_telemetry_reports_born_but_not_transported`
  - `compiler2_reusable_cons_telemetry_reports_birth_transport_and_consumption`
  - `compiler2_reusable_cons_erases_unused_call_argument_before_reuse`
  - `compiler2_reusable_cons_statically_skips_a_returned_source_alias`
- `enum_tier0`, with only its independently owned Map `reduce/2` case skipped,
  remains green on interp, JIT, and AOT.
- Full lib and fixture matrix remain at baseline or better.

ticket is NOT closed by it, mechanism differs):

(1) The reusable_cons_exit_counters #[ignore]d lib test still fails at
head with the byte-identical native-side signature ('backend value
ValueId(0) in FunctionId(32)/Ty(23) must be bound before runtime use'),
verified identical at base 24b228068 in a scratch worktree. fz-kdt.111
fixed the INTERP-side eager evaluation of dead constructions; this
repro is a NATIVE lowering invariant on a value that native itself
expects bound -- a different mechanism. Still the live repro to start
from.

(2) The enum_tier0 claim in this ticket's body ('with the fz-bfh.3 line
skipped it prints eight further values then dies with backend value 0
is unbound') is NOT OBSERVABLE at current heads: base and head behave
identically on all three paths -- interp stops at fz panic
"Enum.EmptyError" (fz-bfh.3, the FIRST blocker) and run/build abort in
_fz_unbox_atom (a DIFFERENT failure than interp's, which the fixture's
one-line deferral rationale does not capture). Re-derive the second
blocker only after fz-bfh.3 lands; update the fixture header's deferral
rationale to name both per-path failures when touched.

(3) Related repair for triangulation: fz-kdt.111 made Lambda/FunctionRef
constructions with Nothing transport layouts lower as Omitted (shared
lowering, native's inline proof deleted as superseded), and taught the
interp's lane-less return contract to treat an env miss on the returned
value as the absence proof. If this ticket's native invariant is the
same proof missing at a THIRD site, check jobs/native.rs's remaining
bound-before-use asserts against transport value_positions first.

title: Ignored reusable-cons return leaves a retained SplitList source unbound
